newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Directionless gilts set to slip to 113-04.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Directionless gilts set to slip to 113-04.

text.p: LIFFE September gilt futures look set to run out of steam on Thursday and are expected to head towards the bottom of their recent trading range around 113-04, technical analsyts said.
"There is quiet a lot of resistance building around 113-25, 27, which there seems to be a stark unwillingness to breach," said Marc Ostwald, technical strategist at London Bond Broking here.
"I would look for gilts to drift back and start testing support again at 113-10, 11 and then 113-04."
At 0705 GMT, September gilts were at 113-17, down 2/32.
Ostwald said 113-04, the low on June 10, marked the bottom of the recent range for gilts and did not expect it to break below that level.
On daily charts 113-10, 11, were the lows on June 6 and 11 respectively, while the resistance levels at 113-25, 27 were the highs on June 5 and 3.
"Even if it does break above there it is not going to go much further," said Ostwald. "We are definitely capped at the moment at Friday and Monday's highs at 114-06, 08."
Technical analysts at Chase in London also said 113-25 was likely to be the limit to the upside.

"Given the preferred (Elliott) wave count calling 114-08 a 'b' wave top it should fail to break 113-25," they said in a research note. "From here it should put the initial 113-04 support under pressure."
They said a break of that level would confirm the high at 114-08 and lead to more weakness near term.
If the contract did break below 113-04 and close below 112-23 it would trigger an acceleration in the downward trend calling for a break of 111-30, Chase analysts said.
From a fundamental perspective, Ostwald said the market price was vacillating between two extremes.
"It doesn't know what to price in at the moment," he said. "People are not willing to commit themselves."

He said the market was undecided on what to expect from the forthcoming British budget on July 2 and whether Britain should be considered as a safehaven in the uncertainly surrounding the European single currency.
At the short end September short sterling futures were at 93.10, up 0.01 from Wednesday.
